title: A monastic rule encodes fault, visible demotion, satisfaction, and conditional re-entry
summary: Rule of Benedict chapter 43 gives a complete status transition: late arrival after a signal leads to last-place placement, public penance, and re-entry; an abbot's permission creates a bounded exception with later satisfaction.

design.mechanism: An institutional rule tracks an actor's status across an event: trigger, sanction/placement, repair, and restored participation, with an explicit authority-conditioned exception.
design.source_example: Rule of Benedict, chapter 43: after the office signal, a late arrival after the Gloria stands last or in a designated place until public penance; at day hours the abbot may permit joining the choir, but satisfaction remains due afterward.
design.target_endpoint: Already admitted complete paragraph cache summarized by GDT928; target text and candidate forms were not opened.

two_readings.name: status-transition rule
consequences: A trigger must precede a visible placement/status change, then a repair or satisfaction stage before normal participation resumes.
The permission exception changes the timing of re-entry but does not erase the later repair obligation.

two_readings.name: ordinary procedural sequence
consequences: Late/early phrases can be temporal instructions without a persistent status state.
A permission clause can replace the following action entirely, with no required repair or re-entry relation.

design.smallest_distinguishing_observation: A later target paragraph would have to preserve a trigger-to-demotion-to-repair-to-reentry chain, and an authority-conditioned branch would alter only re-entry timing. A generic process/list reading predicts no such state carry.
design.nearest_rival: A recipe or service instruction in which ordered actions have no institutional actor status and a permission clause simply selects an alternative action.
assumption_costs: Complete paragraph order and any status/permission markers can be fixed independently.
A monastic regulatory text is a relevant model for a possible metatextual or procedural register.
The source roles remain unglossed target placeholders; no moral or religious meaning is assigned.
design.strongest_likely_failure: No target-visible sanction, authority, or re-entry relation may be independently owned; the chain could then be imposed on any ordered prose.
design.falsifier: On source-frozen complete target paragraphs, a purported status trigger is followed by no stable demotion/repair relation, or permission repeatedly removes rather than delays the repair stage.

primary_sources.locator: Rule of Benedict, chapter 43, On those who come late to the Work of God or to table
primary_sources.source_limit: Modern English translation of the early medieval rule; this card uses its explicit conditional and status sequence, not a target vocabulary.
